Jasmine —

Thanks for sending these over. Quick answers from procurement ops:

- PO ack window: our standard is 3 business days for vendor-accepted orders. We can make an exception for the pilot if Redwood confirms 5 days, but it will be a manual acceptance flag in Ariba.
- Tax ID: yes, Ariba requires an Employer Identification Number (EIN). We’ll need the tax_id and legal_entity name to finish registration.
- EDI/PO: our system accepts line-splitting but requires a consistent SKU mapping. If you attach a sample PO XML we’ll validate it.

I’ve attached our portal evidence checklist (portal_evidence_bundle.pdf). For redlines in the MSA, legal will review — I’ve looped them in separately but they typically expect liability caps and data residency language to be clarified for vendors handling production data.

Reviewed the MSA redlines. High-level guidance:

- Liability cap: propose a compromise cap of "direct damages up to the total fees paid under the Order Form for the 12-month period" for the pilot. This is narrower than our standard but should be acceptable for a time-limited pilot and reduce procurement friction.
- Indemnity: narrow to third-party IP claims only; push back on broad product liability language.
- Data residency / access: add a clause that production data for the pilot will be processed in our US region; any cross-border processing must be scheduled and approved.

Operational asks for onboarding (assign to Marissa):
1) Prepare a signatory matrix with delegated signer names and email addresses.
2) Confirm SFTP host/IP and folder naming convention for PO/Invoice exchange.
3) Provide a sample PO XML (Jasmine, ask MedixProcure to send) for EDI validation.

If MedixProcure insists on the 3-day PO ack, we can accept for the pilot with the caveat that it may require a manual confirmation step in Ariba; include a short service level note in the Order Form.

I’ll draft tracked changes and share within the hour.

Hi Jasmine / Sally —

Thanks for the details. Answers below:

- Pilot PO ack SLA: Yes, Ariba supports per-vendor custom acceptance rules. Your account admin can set a "vendor-specific SLA" flag. For pilot cases we recommend using the "manual acceptance" workflow (see: Admin > Procurement Rules > Manual Acknowledgements). This prevents a global policy change.

- Evidence bundle: Ariba will accept a partial registration (EIN + signatory matrix + W-9). The remaining documents (insurance certs, SOC reports) can be uploaded post-activation but will remain as open gating items in the vendor record until received. Note that some buyers enforce hard gating, in which case the buyer must set the gating policy to "onboarding allowed with pending evidence." Ask MedixProcure procurement to set that flag.

- PO XML validation: please send a sample XML to vendor-validation@ariba.com. Include a note about expected SKU mapping and whether line-splitting is acceptable. We’ll run it through our test harness and return a validation report in 24–48 hours.

Best,
Ariba Support
